name: Letting Go
intro: We hold on to so much. Grudges. Regrets. Expectations. Old versions of ourselves.
Letting go isn't giving up. It's making room.
Room for something lighter. Something truer.
Take a deep breath in. And as you exhale, imagine your hands slowly opening.
Let's begin to loosen what no longer serves you.
body: Think of something you've been gripping tightly.
A resentment. A memory you keep replaying. A version of events you insist on.
Feel how much energy it takes to hold it.
Your hand is clenched around it. Your jaw is tight. Your shoulders are lifted.
What if you loosened your grip? Not all the way. Just a fraction.
Letting go doesn't mean it didn't matter.
It doesn't mean it was okay. It doesn't mean you've forgotten.
It means you've decided that carrying it is costing more than keeping it.
You can honor what happened and still set it down.
Breathe out. Feel the weight shift.
Think of a person you need to release. Someone whose actions still live in you.
Not to forgive them. Not yet, if you're not ready. That's okay.
Just to untangle their story from yours.
Their choices were theirs. Your life is yours.
You don't have to carry what they put down long ago.
Now think of an old version of yourself you've been mourning.
The person you were before. Before the loss. Before the change.
That person did their best. And they brought you here.
But you are not them anymore. And pretending you are keeps you stuck.
Thank them. Honor them. And let them rest.
Imagine standing by a river. In your hands you hold stones.
Each stone is labeled. One says control. One says perfection. One says fear.
One by one, place them in the water.
Watch them sink. Watch the river carry on, undisturbed.
Your hands are lighter. Your breath is deeper. Something has shifted.
closing: Letting go is not a single act. It's a practice.
Some things you'll need to release more than once. That's normal.
But today, you loosened something. You made space.
That space will fill with something better. Trust that.
Open your eyes. You are lighter than you were before.
